title: The bounded non-full filtered subcategory system and its canonical colimit diagram
statement: Use the ordinary categories, filteredness and chosen colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with explicit universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. For a small category $J$, a subcategory $K$ consists of subsets $O_K\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}J$ and $E_K\subseteq\coprod_{x,y\in J}\operatorname{Hom}_J(x,y)$, with endpoints of selected arrows in $O_K$, all identities of $O_K$ in $E_K$, and closure under composition. Its category has objects $O_K$ and the selected arrows, and $i_K:K\to J$ is inclusion. Inclusion of both subsets orders these subcategories. For any small cardinal $\kappa$, define $P_{J,\kappa}=\{K:K\text{ is filtered},\ |E_K|<\kappa\}$ with its induced partial order; it is a small type in the universe of $J$. For a locally small category $A$ with all small colimits and $X:J\to A$, define $Y_X:P_{J,\kappa}\to A$ by $Y_X(K)=\operatorname{colim}(i_K^*X)$ and the unique transition maps taking every inner coprojection to the corresponding coprojection for a larger subcategory. Define $q_X:\operatorname{colim}_{K\in P_{J,\kappa}}Y_X(K)\to\operatorname{colim}_JX$ by descending the ambient colimit cocone first over each $K$ and then over $P_{J,\kappa}$; thus $q_X$ composed with the outer and inner coprojections equals the ambient coprojection. No fullness, regularity or filteredness of $J$ is required for this definition.
